target_customer: Online platforms and market research panels that need to filter bots and AI agents from real users (survey panels, financial sign-ups, ticketing)
problem: CAPTCHAs add friction and increasingly fail against AI agents, so platforms cannot cheaply tell humans from bots.
product_category: bot detection and human verification API

founders.name: Mayank Agrawal
education: Princeton University, PhD in cognitive science and AI
founders.background_notes: YC page says his work was published in Science, PNAS and Psychological Review.

founders.name: Matt Hardy
education: University of Toronto, statistics and economics
founders.background_notes: YC page says he worked in data science and econometrics before the PhD.

technical_complexity.rationale: Behavioral biometrics and device and network signal modeling needs research skill, but a small team of cognitive scientists could ship an API; the 99 percent detection claim is the company's own and unverified.

defensibility.rationale: Detection quality depends on accumulated behavioral data and research credibility, but the category has many CAPTCHA and bot defense vendors and claims are self-reported.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents were already offering invisible bot detection; no source shows them acquiring or copying this company.

market_need_then: Search results show bot and AI agent traffic and survey fraud as a live pain by 2025; no source dated near the 2023 batch was found, so need at founding is inferred only from the YC page pitch.

branding.domain_note: Company site is poh.org; earlier brand name Roundtable used roundtable.ai (YC page slug roundtable).

identity.logo: minimal black and white marks per site fetch
identity.visual_style: minimal, mostly black and white with red and green status icons

rebrands.why: Company site says formerly Roundtable AI, now Proof of Human, PBC; Roundtable's own site lists Proof of Human as its product, so the exact change date and reason are not sourced.

brand_strength.rationale: Name is a generic category phrase also used by World and others, per Biometric Update coverage; no evidence of community or press about the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Proof of Human is active with a five person team as of the YC page and no reported acquisition, shutdown or layoffs. It started as Roundtable and now sells an invisible bot verification API; its public traction claims are 10M plus monthly sessions and named customers like Stanford Psychology. Funding is not publicly confirmed, so its trajectory cannot be judged beyond staying alive and shipping.
notes: Dealroom lists a single 125k seed round with no investors or date; unverified and likely the YC investment, so not recorded as a round. A YC profile snippet says Brickyard Ventures is a backer, seen only in search results. No competitor source dated near mid 2023 was found; later Roundtable blog comparisons with reCAPTCHA, hCaptcha, Turnstile and Arkose Labs date from 2025.
